title: Designing a Handoff That Does Not Depend on Memory
excerpt: How a sales-to-delivery handoff can be made explicit, checkable and useful before any automation is introduced.

sections.heading: Context
paragraphs: The team was moving quickly, but delivery questions kept coming back to sales. The process appeared efficient from the outside because everyone knew the work; the hidden cost was repeated clarification.

sections.heading: Diagnosis
paragraphs: The root problem was not a lack of tools. It was that the handoff itself was undefined. There was no shared minimum information set and no clear point at which responsibility changed hands.

sections.heading: Approach
paragraphs: First define the handoff, then define the data required to make it useful, then decide which parts are worth automating. The sequence matters.
sections.imageAlt: Structured process map used to define the handoff

sections.heading: Outcome
paragraphs: The resulting structure gives sales a clear completion point and engineering a predictable starting point. The process becomes easier to measure because the handoff is visible rather than implicit.
